verdict.rationale: BugSnag documents release tracking: you can identify which release an error was introduced in, filter by release, see release annotations on the timeline, and create builds and releases via the CLI. Stack traces can also link to source lines on some platforms. Nothing in the evidence shows commit association or suspect-commit attribution on an issue. Missing for 10: suspect-commit identification, documented commit/SCM association per issue, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can associate errors with releases and commits so each issue shows the release it first appeared in and the suspect commit that likely caused it

citations.quote: filter your dashboard by release and identify which release errors were introduced in.
see release annotations on the timeline to correlate new versions with changes in error rates.
Allows you to create a build within BugSnag to enrich releases shown in the BugSnag dashboard.
Stack traces will link directly to view the line of code (on some platforms).
